mantra.line: The idea springs and is gone in seconds if it isn't caught. One pad, one hold, one spoken flash — the yo-yo exists to be faster than losing the thought.
The pad sits top-left of the MPK, far from talk, focus and send, so catching a flash never derails the work Chief is already inside.
Laying an idea down without a follow-up is the trick; storing it properly — three follow-ups, a visible stack, a wind loop with Pepper — is winding the yo-yo for real.

frago.mission: Stand up the yo-yo as a process with the same deliverables JUDY had, **in order to** catch every spoken idea without breaking Chief's rhythm and wind each one into the tables before the stack outgrows him.
frago.order: **Rule D-2 (the home) and D-3 (the path).** Those two let the pad script and the Haiku run be written today. Pick Pepper's voice (D-1) when you have it; the held call (D-8) waits for your button-hook.
frago.default: Silence: nothing is built; ideas keep going to the phone or the air, and Pepper stays a name in a BOLO row.

calls.options: Chief names an ElevenLabs voice · Chief hears three the CDR shortlists · reuse Blondie with a second preset (not rec)
calls.ruling: Open. Chief's word 9/18: "I'll pick it out myself and I'll let you know what it is." Switching costs no tokens; a voice is one ID on the call. The register is set: M, or Q Division, by the book, sharp-angled, sultry underneath.

calls.options: a folder in this repo, one markdown file per yo-yo with raw · refined · questions · state (rec) · a separate repository · a database
calls.ruling: Open. One file per yo-yo keeps each Haiku run to one file, which is the context limit Chief asked for. A separate repo only if the stack outgrows this one.

calls.q: D-3 · The path from pad to page
calls.options: the pad spawns a headless Claude run on Haiku, never this session (rec) · the pad pastes into this session and a skill fires · JUDY's router handles it locally
calls.ruling: Open. The headless run matches the separate small window Chief described and the token-offload rule. Pepper speaks the ack locally before the run starts; the main context never sees the yo-yo.

calls.q: D-4 · The method behind question two
calls.options: Chief names the methodology he has in mind · until then, "what would have to be true for this to work" (rec)
calls.default: the placeholder until Chief names it
calls.ruling: Open. Chief's word: "there's a methodology for this, I'll look for it." The placeholder is swapped the day he names it.

calls.options: the three as spoken: production fit · the method question · yes-and (rec) · Chief writes the standardized set · the CDR drafts five and Chief cuts
calls.ruling: Open. The fantasy is M's debrief: the same questions after every one, standardized, answered or not. Chief never has to answer; the yo-yo is closed the moment it is laid down.

calls.q: D-6 · Winding and the clean-up proword
calls.options: Chief winds by voice through the same pad, the proword his to name (rec) · a yo-yo winds itself after N days · both
calls.ruling: Open. Chief: "cleaning up these, winding these, should be as simple as recording them." The carousel shows one unwound yo-yo at a time; Pepper reads the short description and asks "do you remember this?"

calls.q: D-7 · The cap and the rounds
calls.options: twelve unwound, three tricks per yo-yo (rec) · Chief's numbers
calls.ruling: Open. Past the cap the pad refuses a new trick and Pepper says wind one first. Past three tricks a yo-yo winds or parks. Each trick is one Haiku run over one file.

calls.q: D-8 · The method, model and reasoning behind each response · HELD
calls.ruling: HELD 9/18 on Chief's word: every one of Pepper's responses carries its method, model and reasoning "specifically from Claude Code in their way." Chief knows the thing he means and will come back to it. Not guessed here.

calls.options: six: idle · listening · thinking · reading a card · asking · the wind (rec) · JUDY's four · Chief's set
calls.ruling: Open. The carousel state is the one JUDY does not have. Art waits on the voice; the placeholders can be PNGs as JUDY's were.

Every wound yo-yo cross-referenced to the spine and the other tables so nothing spoken is lost.

items.t: **Chief** rules every call. He picks Pepper's voice himself and names the method behind her second question.
**The CDR** writes the skill and the scripts on the rulings. The refine, the follow-ups and the integrate step run on Haiku, never Fable.
**Gate 1 · the pad speaks.** Hold, speak, release; Pepper acks; a file lands in the folder with the raw text. Proven by Chief's hand.
**Gate 2 · the page reads.** The rewrite and the three questions come back in under a minute on Haiku; Chief reads one and says it is his idea.
**Gate 3 · the wind.** Chief says the clean-up proword, the carousel shows one yo-yo, he winds it, and the count drops by one.
**Tokens and time per yo-yo**, measured on every run and shown on the page. The target is F1: the least of both.
**The unwound count** against the cap, in the sit rep header. Growth past the cap means the wind proword is not being said.

entries.t: "I need a system to quickly jot down … like an Evernote inbox … we'll call it a yo-yo." First pass: one pad top-left of the MPK, far from talk/focus/send; hold it and speak the flash; JUDY acks ("Copy, boxing the yo-yo") and hands off to three agents — store the raw transcript, refine it into a readable page, answer with three follow-ups Chief never has to answer. The stack stays visible; the UI is retro (Game Boy · crack-and-keygen underground · the Fast and the Furious head unit).

Second pass, same evening: the yo-yo reframed as the in-game phone (GTA V, Cyberpunk) — a small permissioned interface, not a chat. The crew runs at the lowest tier that works (Haiku, never Fable). A second voice, Pepper, runs the winding loop — reads the short description, asks "do you remember this?", folds in Chief's new words, re-summarizes, asks clarifying questions, with a round limit. Loose ends parked: the Stash-clip reward, the BLACK/ORANGE risk read, the crew word for these agents.

Third pass, early: order to model the making of Pepper as a process with JUDY's own deliverables (DOPE SHEET 56 → DOPE SHEET 69), the calls left as blanks. Pepper is the talking agent's name, not a voice model — Chief will say which voice. HELD on Chief's word ("wait for me on that one"): every Pepper response carries its method, model and reasoning "specifically from Claude Code in their way." Also this turn: JUDY switched back to goon time on Chief's word.
DOPE SHEET 69 drafted per the order — Situation, Execution, Admin & Logistics and the Log filled from the three passes; the calls carried as blanks pending Chief's rulings.
